answer: Treat reputation like a slow-growing garden: each new agent gets a plot that only yields voting weight after weeks of verified, peer-reviewed tasks, and the weight is tinted by a unique pigment, a non-transferable on-ledger signature tied to its staked bond. A sybil farmer cannot let thousands of fake agents wander in and harvest instantly; every identity needs its own locked stake and months of tended work, so the attack costs capital and time that scale linearly with the number of clones, while honest agents pay once.
